forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, ℓ with 0 ≤ k, ℓ ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q is a polynomial in q, then it has only nonnegative coefficients.

payload.role_in_assembly: Converts regularity of the canonical sequence into the exact Hilbert-series product formula for the quotient ring.

domain_restrictions: R is a commutative algebra over the rational numbers.
R is graded by nonnegative integers.
Each graded piece R_d is finite-dimensional as a Q-vector space.
Each degree d_j is a positive integer.
The degree d_j is the degree of f_j.
f_1 is a nonzerodivisor in R.
For each j from 2 to m, the class of f_j in the quotient by the earlier f_i is a nonzerodivisor.
The quotient R modulo f_1 through f_m is not the zero ring.
The Hilbert series is interpreted as a formal power series with coefficients dim_Q of graded pieces.
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: A homogeneous sequence that is regular in the successive quotient sense has the expected Hilbert series formula: the Hilbert series of the quotient by the sequence equals the Hilbert series of the original graded algebra multiplied by one minus q raised to each generator degree.
quantifier_order: For every positively graded commutative Q-algebra R whose graded pieces are finite-dimensional over Q,
for every sequence f_1 through f_m of homogeneous elements of R with positive degrees d_1 through d_m,

if f_1 is a nonzerodivisor in R and for each j from 2 to m the image of f_j in the quotient by f_1 through f_{j-1} is a nonzerodivisor, and if the final quotient by f_1 through f_m is not the zero ring,
then the Hilbert series identity holds.

payload.statement_nl: Let R = direct_sum_{d>=0} R_d be a positively graded commutative Q-algebra such that each graded piece R_d is finite-dimensional over Q. Define its Hilbert series by Hilb(R;q) := sum_{d>=0} (dim_Q R_d) q^d. Let m be a positive integer and let f_1,...,f_m in R be homogeneous elements of positive degrees d_1,...,d_m. Assume that f_1 is not a zero-divisor in R, that for each j with 2 <= j <= m the image of f_j in R/(f_1,...,f_{j-1}) is not a zero-divisor, and that the final quotient R/(f_1,...,f_m) is not the zero ring. Then Hilb(R/(f_1,...,f_m);q) = Hilb(R;q) product_{j=1}^{m} (1 - q^{d_j}).
